subtype: Approach: releases a small first version and asks users for feedback [Action]
passage: I'm Sonali, and last month I did something I had never done: I sent out an app before it was ready. I used to dream of two hundred questions, a leaderboard and cartoon levels. Then Seema said in class, "Just show us something." So I put in ten questions and sent the link to eleven classmates. I did not ask anything. I just watched the results. Nearly everyone skipped the two history questions and played all three cricket ones twice. That told me more than any guess of mine. So the next weekend I wrote fifteen more cricket questions and left history alone. I am still a little embarrassed about how plain the first version looked. But I am glad I sent it.

qa.q: How many questions were in the first version?
qa.a: The first version had ten questions.

qa.q: How does Sonali feel looking back at the first version?
qa.a: Sonali feels a little embarrassed about how plain it looked, but glad it was sent out.

qa.q: What else could Sonali do to learn what classmates like?
qa.a: Sonali could ask two or three classmates to say aloud what they would change while they play, along with watching which questions get skipped.

qa.q: How might Seema see the app now?
qa.a: Seema, who asked to be shown something, may be pleased to have played it and might like that the cricket topic grew.

grounding: Shows a teenager releasing ten questions first, watching what classmates skip and adding more of the popular topic.
